{#i88x} # Discussion

{#c83u} In this cross-sectional survey of 262 pregnant women coming for their regular clinical visits in one center in Switzerland, we found a prevalence of tobacco products at 7.6%, ENDS at 0.8%, NRT at 0.4%, and cannabinoid use at 3.8%.

{#twdy} Previously conducted studies observed the prevalence of tobacco use among pregnant women in Switzerland to vary between 7.0% and 21.0% [@w:w21]. This is in line with the current study showing a prevalence of 7.6%. In the French perinatal survey, 16.6% of women smoked tobacco in their third trimester of pregnancy in 2016, which then decreased to 12.2% in 2021 [@w:w22]. {#z9v1} # Introduction

{#zyg0} Smoking tobacco in pregnancy is a prevalent, modifiable risk factor for infant mortality and morbidity [@w:w1]. The global prevalence of smoking during pregnancy was estimated at 1.8%, with Europe reporting a prevalence of 8.1% . In the USA, 5.4% of women who gave birth in 2021 reported smoking while being pregnant [@w:w2]. In 2022, 8.3% of women giving birth in Australia admitted to smoking during the first 20 weeks of pregnancy, with 71% of them continuing to smoke throughout their pregnancy [@w:w3]. Smoking during pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of several adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, such as placenta previa, placental abruption, premature rupture of membranes, stillbirth, preterm birth, and small for gestational age [@w:w4]. However, smoking cessation can help reduce these adverse effects [@w:w5].

{#b0dl} Smoking cessation counseling has been beneficial in supporting pregnant women to quit tobacco use, but some might need additional support with smoking cessation aids to quit smoking [@w:w6]. In addition to nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) and pharmacotherapy (Varenicline or Bupropion), women view electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) as an aid for smoking cessation during pregnancy [@w:w7].
